qualifiedDispositions.reasonJa: A–K §Elnaam, lines 2509–2513, says the same father/sons and cites 1 Chronicles 11:46. Null is a false negative; offer shared-section candidate.

A–K §Elpaal, lines 2533–2537, says son of Hushim and wife of Shaharaim while cautioning that Shaharaim’s relation to Benjamin is unstated. Null is a false negative; do not add unstated Benjamin lineage.
A–K §§Elpalet/Elpelet, lines 2538–2548 redirect to two separate entries; notes many variant spellings. Candidate is relevant but does not by itself prove the two WEB occurrences are one person.
A–K §Elzabad, lines 2555–2562 distinguishes two Elzabads and explicitly identifies this exact 26:7 porter. Null is a false negative.
A–K §Ephlal, lines 2582–2586, identifies Ephlal as Zabad’s son in a Jerahmeelite genealogy. Null is a false negative.

Grouped Wikipedia search did not locate an exact A–K/L–Z subsection; a non-Wikipedia “List of minor biblical tribes” page surfaced, so it is not counted as a Wikipedia fit. No claim that no article exists.
Grouped Wikipedia searches surfaced David’s Mighty Warriors list with Naarai ben Ezbai, but no fitting individual article/shared subsection was verified. Do not call article absence proven.

A–K search §Chelub/Ezri adjacent entry and the list’s Ezer entries show multiple namesakes; no direct exact entry for Ephraim’s Ezer found in the reviewed excerpt. Current null should be reconsidered against 1 Chronicles figures list, not substituted with another Ezer.
A–K line 2030 explicitly names Ezri son of Chelub with the same role/reference. Null is a false negative.
A–K §Gamul, line 2693 says the twentieth division, conflicting with fixed WEB 24:17. Existing note flags the disagreement, which is appropriate; keep WEB as profile basis.
A–K §Gatam lines 2694–2698 compares Genesis/Chronicles and notes Genesis 36:16 calls Gatam and others clans. Current cautious profile is acceptable; avoid asserting a settled individual ontology.

Exact-name grouped search did not identify a Wikipedia subsection for this Geshan. Search results for Geshan are ambiguous with other biblical name forms; no-fit remains limited to the pages/queries checked.
Wikipedia searches did not locate a target-specific Girgashite section; Hivites is not interchangeable. Keep explicit collective type and do not claim the ethnicity’s exact historical identity.
A–K §Hachmoni lines 2806–2810 states Jehiel is Hachmoni’s son, a scribe, and tutor. It supports the relation, not a certain individual biography for Hachmoni.

Hadad (Bible) lines 105–110 lists several Hadads/Hadar, including the Edomite king whose wife is Mehetabel. The notes at 1:50 association support relevance, but the article is a name-set and does not resolve spellings/identity across traditions.

Search results found the Mighty Warriors list with “Mibhar ben Hagri”; the Wikipedia L–Z Mibhar listing associates a Hagarene form, but that does not establish this father’s identity. Null/hold is more accurate than identity link.

Searches found Bible dictionaries and concordance material but did not verify a Wikipedia individual article/body subsection. A Wikipedia shared subsection may exist; keep this null classification provisional.
No target-specific Wikipedia article/section found in the queries checked. Preserve the exact WEB genealogy and note that the successive “his son” chain is textually stated.
A–K Maacah related references did not establish a dedicated Hanan section for this specific warrior in the reviewed body. Search result match alone is insufficient; no identity link.
A–K §Hareph lines 2953–2957 gives the same father/son relation and says it may denote a group. Null is a false negative; profile’s caveat is sensible.
A–K §Harum lines 2985–2989 says he is father of Aharhel. Null is a false negative.
Searches found Havilah geographic entries but no direct article evidence for this Joktan descendant; a land/region page is not a person identity match.
Target-specific Wikipedia page/section not found in the searches checked; namesake hits are unrelated. Not a universal absence claim.
A–K §Heber lines 3080–3086 covers Jael’s Kenite husband and Asher’s grandson; neither matches Benjamin’s Heber. No target match found.
A–K Hebron lines 3087–3091 points to Caleb’s son in 1 Chronicles 2:42–43, a different person. Null is appropriate unless a separate fit is found; do not use the city article.
No active link; evidence must retain the hold/identity-uncertain reason. Not counted as a “no article” result.
A–K §Hezekiah lines 3156–3157 records a son of Neariah and notes Hizkiah variants. Null is a false negative; add shared-section link only with name/gate correctly bounded.
A–K §Hezron lines 3168–3175 distinguishes Hezron son of Reuben from Hezron son of Judah/Perez. Null omits an exact match.
A–K page and dedicated Hilkiah results mainly identify the later high priest; no exact target section verified. Keep namesake uncertainty explicit.

Hivites article lines 121–123 describes the people and says their precise historical identity is unresolved; article also carries an unsourced-content warning. The draft must not claim a settled modern ethnic identification.
No exact Wikipedia person subsection found in checked queries. Keep text-bound kinship and avoid resolving the syntax beyond WEB.
A–K §Hotham lines 3246–3250 explicitly says the 7:32 figure is called Helem in verse 35. Null is a false negative; link note must preserve translational/identity caveat.
No exact Wikipedia person subsection verified; similarly named Hul/Hulites results are not sufficient proof.

Dedicated Hur article has multiple traditions; the fit is plausible but not sufficient to erase the internal WEB genealogical tension. Null is a false negative only if the relation is stated with that caveat.
A–K search did not verify a target-specific entry; similarly named Hiram/Huram of Solomon’s era is a different person.
A–K §Hushim lines 3274–3278 treats the Dan genealogy in Genesis 46:23/Numbers 26:42, not this 1 Chronicles 7:12 Hushim; do not connect as same person.
No fitting exact Wikipedia article/body section verified in checked searches.
A–K §Igal lines 3315–3322 explicitly identifies Igal son of Shemaiah as the 1 Chronicles 3:22 figure and notes the KJV spelling “Igeal”. Null is a false negative.
